pool.text: Mughal emperor Humayun passed through the Quetta region while fleeing to Safavid Iran.
The Quetta region came under the authority of the Afghan Hotak dynasty.
Ahmad Shah Durrani incorporated Quetta into the Afghan state.
British traveller Charles Masson described Quetta as a mud-walled fort with mud houses.
General John Jacob urged the British government to occupy Quetta for frontier defence.
Formal British control was established through a lease arrangement with the Khan of Kalat.
British census records confirmed that Kasi Pashtuns remained the principal indigenous landholders.
Quetta was almost entirely destroyed by a major earthquake resulting in widespread devastation.
Following the creation of Pakistan, Quetta became the provincial capital of Balochistan.
Quetta is the ninth largest city in Pakistan with an estimated population.
